items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' — the call opened with 'Hello, this is Amy. How can I help you?' and went straight into a profile hunt with no roadmap or timeframe set.
Never asked 'how are you today?' or any warm-up question.
Never confirmed or asked for the move date, even after the customer said 'I thought we are booked' — the date was never established on a call whose whole purpose was booking readiness.

No quote recap. Amy could see 'the quote was sent to her earlier, like around 2:39' but never read the number, the mover/truck count, or the estimated hours back to the decision-maker who was on the phone asking what to expect.
No hourly rate, no 'pricing is super simple' framing, no what's-included list (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools), no trip fee, no 'no hidden fees' pitch.
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — the single biggest miss, because the customer twice raised damage anxiety about white couches and white mattresses going into storage.

No clock explanation at all — no 'clock starts on-site,' no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments — despite Amy herself raising the time-and-money theme when she suggested pre-disassembling beds.

Moving-blanket policy explained inconsistently: '$14 per piece' as a rental, then 'when you give us the moving blankets back... we will refund you the deposit.' The customer heard '$40' and asked twice 'for how long?' before Amy landed on 'it doesn't matter how long.' He agreed to rent them without ever being told the total or whether it is a charge or a refundable hold.

'We don't use the job number sir. We don't use a job number' — repeated flatly after the customer twice offered it as a way to find the record, while Amy spent roughly three minutes of the call spelling names over a bad line.
Storage-unit size never captured — the customer flagged it himself on the way out ('I know you asked me the size of the storage') and Amy let the call end without getting it.
Never asked about packing needs, box count, stairs, or access/parking at either the origin or the storage facility.

Missed the stated moving stressor. The customer explained his worry about white upholstery getting dirty in storage and Amy answered 'I see. Sure, sure.' — no reassurance, no No Worries tie-in, no commitment to note it on the job.
Booking attempt made but not closed or scheduled forward. When the customer said he would call back, Amy accepted it without proposing a specific time or offering to hold a date.
No 'no deposit required' mention, no BOLDED-details framing for the confirmation email, and no 'reply with any corrections.'
Customer's name used only once ('Anything else, Richard?') — short of the 3+ standard.
top_strength: Amy handled a genuinely bad call well on the mechanics she chose to work. She stayed calm through a cutting-in-and-out line, said plainly 'I can barely hear you sir. Are you currently driving?' rather than guessing, and waited while he parked — that is the right instinct and it protected the accuracy of everything after it. She then answered a rapid run of pre-booking FAQs cleanly and honestly: shrink wrap plus moving blankets before loading, mattresses wrapped, TVs unmounted, and the honest boundary 'we don't seal the walls... we don't do carpentry' instead of overpromising. She also volunteered a real efficiency tip unprompted: 'if you want to save time, I would suggest you disassemble the beds in advance to save time and money by the end of the day.'
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: Amy had the decision-maker on the phone with a live quote already sent and never recapped it. When she found the record she should have said, 'Richard, I have your quote right here — it's four movers and a truck from 1711 Netto to the storage unit at 4649 Texas 276, estimated at X hours, which comes to about $Y at $Z per mover per hour, and there is no deposit to hold the date. Want me to lock in a day right now?' Instead the pricing conversation never happened and the call ended with 'I will confirm and call you back' — a quoted, walkthrough-complete job left unbooked. Second priority: he handed her the No Worries opening twice by worrying out loud about white couches and white mattresses going into storage, and she answered 'I see. Sure, sure.' The line she needed was 'That's exactly what our No Worries Damage Coverage is for — up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damage, and I'm noting the white upholstery on your job right now so the crew knows to double-wrap it.' Practice pairing every stated fear with the differentiator that answers it. Business risks to fix in EMMA today: (1) the moving-blanket terms were left genuinely ambiguous — '$14 per piece' rental versus a refunded deposit — and the customer committed to renting without a total, which is a billing dispute waiting to happen; get the policy stated one way and confirmed in writing. (2) Amy verbally committed to 'inform the movers to bring moving blanket' and to the white-upholstery wrap request, and neither is confirmed as logged on the job. (3) The storage-unit size is still unknown, which is a load-planning gap on a job that is about to be booked. Also worth noting: two profiles for one household (Richard and Florence) nearly caused a duplicate-record mess, and Amy's fix was to tell him to always give Florence's name — a workaround, not a merge.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and professional under real line trouble, and she closed warmly with 'Thank you. Drive safely' — but the language was largely transactional, the repeated 'We don't use the job number' landed curt, and the customer's clearly stated worry about his white furniture drew only 'I see. Sure, sure.'
audio_review_reason: Call quality was poor for a sustained stretch ('it's cutting in and out, I can barely understand') and the customer's side of the transcript is heavily garbled, so tone during the repeated can't-hear-you exchanges and during the missed damage-worry moment cannot be judged from text alone.
